His words, Exalted is He: "So let them worship the Lord of this House" (﴿فَلْيَعْبُدُوا رَبَّ هَذا البَيْتِ﴾), that is, let them declare Him one, "who fed them against hunger" (﴿الَّذِي أطْعَمَهم مِن جُوعٍ﴾), that is, after hunger, just as you say "I clothed you after nakedness." This is because Allah secured them in the Sanctuary, so they were not molested on their journeys, and that was the cause of their being fed after the hunger they had been in. ʿAṭāʾ narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: "They were in hardship and famine until Hāshim gathered them for the two journeys, and they would divide their profit between the rich and the poor until they became wealthy." (p-242)

His words, Exalted is He: "and secured them against fear" (﴿وَآمَنَهم مِن خَوْفٍ﴾). This is because they were secure in the Sanctuary: if they stayed, it protected them, and if they travelled, it was said: "These are the people of the Sanctuary," so no one would confront them.
